question_text: Draw a line, say AB, take a point C outside it. Through C, draw a line parallel to AB using ruler and compasses only.

question_image.description: Diagrams showing steps to draw a parallel line using a compass and ruler.

answer_text: The steps of construction are as follows: (i) Draw a line AB. Take a point P on it. Take a point C outside this line. Join C to P. (ii) Taking P as centre and with a convenient radius, draw an arc intersecting line AB at point D and PC at point E. (iii) Taking C as centre and with the same radius as before, draw an arc FG intersecting PC at H. (iv) Adjust the compasses up to the length of DE. Without changing the opening of compasses and taking H as the centre, draw an arc to intersect the previously drawn arc FG at point I. (v) Join the points C and I to draw a line 'l'.

steps.description: Draw line AB and point C outside it.
Join C to P on line AB.
Draw an arc from P intersecting AB and PC.
Draw an arc from C with the same radius intersecting PC.
Draw an arc from H to intersect the previous arc.
Join points C and I to complete the parallel line.

final_answer: This is the required line which is parallel to line AB.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of geometric construction and multiple steps.

question_text: Draw a line l. Draw a perpendicular to l at any point on l. On this perpendicular choose a point X, 4 cm away from l. Through X, draw a line m parallel to l.

(ii) Adjusting the compasses up to the length of 4 cm, draw an arc to intersect this perpendicular at point X. Choose any point Y on line l. Join X to Y. (iii) Taking Y as centre and with a convenient radius, draw an arc intersecting l at A and XY at B.

question_text: Construct an equilateral triangle of side 5.5 cm.
answer_text: An equilateral triangle of side 5.5 cm has to be constructed. We know that all sides of an equilateral triangle are of equal length. Therefore, a triangle ABC has to be constructed with AB = BC = CA = 5.5 cm. The steps of construction are as follows: (i) Draw a line segment BC of length 5.5 cm. (ii) Taking point B as centre, draw an arc of 5.5 cm radius. (iii) Taking point C as centre, draw an arc of 5.5 cm radius to meet the previous arc at point A.

steps.description: Draw a line segment BC of length 5.5 cm.
Taking point B as centre, draw an arc of 5.5 cm radius.
Taking point C as centre, draw an arc of 5.5 cm radius to meet the previous arc at point A.

final_answer: Thus, triangle ABC is the required equilateral triangle.

question_text: Draw ΔPQR with PQ = 4 cm, QR = 3.5 cm and PR = 4 cm. What type of triangle is this?

question_image.description: Diagram showing the construction steps for triangle PQR.

answer_text: The steps of construction are as follows: (i) Draw a line segment QR of length 3.5 cm. (ii) Taking point Q as centre, draw an arc of 4 cm radius. (iii) Taking point R as centre, draw an arc of 4 cm radius to intersect the previous arc at point P. ΔPQR is the required triangle. As the two sides of this triangle are of the same length (PQ = PR), therefore, ΔPQR is an isosceles triangle.

steps.description: Draw a line segment QR of length 3.5 cm.
Taking point Q as centre, draw an arc of 4 cm radius.
Taking point R as centre, draw an arc of 4 cm radius to intersect the previous arc at point P.

final_answer: Therefore, ΔPQR is an isosceles triangle.
